label: PBI report build
info: Builds the pbi_* tables of eu_report/pbi_report/report from the CSV files in the data lake (machine names, shift names, calendar, plan OPT, time utilisation). No API calls. Needs the Config tab.

name: [1] TRIGGER & TASK SETTINGS
info: STAGE 1 - TRIGGER AND TASK SETTINGS. Builds the Power BI tables of eu_report/pbi_report/report from the CSV files in the data lake. Tables: pbi_machine_names (Machine Names files, filters of the report queries), pbi_shift_naming (the distinct shifts), pbi_calendar (generated), pbi_plan_opt and pbi_time_utilisation (the month files of the sites, with Glidepaths targets and shift names). The inject payload is the job: {"tables": [...], "sites": [...], "from": "YYYY-MM", "to": "YYYY-MM"}; a missing list means all, missing months mean last month and this month. Nothing is written while the table is true in DRY_RUN of 1.1.

name: 1.1 TASK SETTINGS (edit here)
1.2 Start jobs
[2] MACHINE NAMES: FILES
info: STAGE 2 - one message per site: the folder eu_report/reference/machine_names/site=<Site>/ is listed, the newest .csv file is read and parsed (header row, one message with all rows), and the rows of the site are built with the filters of the report queries (Hull: no "GT4 - Auto", Dept Dries Pack or Liquids Pack; Nottingham: Area SD Packing or Strepsils Packing; Weinheim: all). A site without a file gives a failed item: then nothing is written for the table.

name: 2.1 Set site folder
2.2 Pick the file
2.3 Build machine rows
[3] pbi_machine_names
info: STAGE 3 - the join waits for the items of all sites, collect puts the rows in one list, decide writes nothing when a site failed or in dry-run mode, then parquet, path and write object. Unique Machine Name = machine name + "-" + site, as in the report. One file for all sites.

name: 3.1 Collect pbi_machine_names
3.2 Decide pbi_machine_names
3.3 Set pbi_machine_names path
[4] SHIFT NAMES: FILE
info: STAGE 4 - the folder eu_report/reference/shift_naming/site=All/ is listed, the newest .csv file (Shift Patterns Provideam EU, columns ShiftName and Shift) is read and parsed, one row per line.

name: 4.1 Set shift folder
4.2 Pick the file
4.3 Build shift rows
[5] pbi_shift_naming
info: STAGE 5 - collect, keep every shift once (the report takes the distinct Shift values: Afternoon, Blue, Day, Gold, Green, Night, Red), decide, parquet, path, write object.

name: 5.1 Collect pbi_shift_naming
5.2 Keep distinct shifts
5.3 Decide pbi_shift_naming
5.4 Set pbi_shift_naming path
[6] pbi_calendar
info: STAGE 6 - generated, no file: one row per date from CALENDAR_START to CALENDAR_END in 1.1 (2011-01-01 to 2050-12-31 as in the report, 14610 rows), Monday week start, week number as DAX WEEKNUM(date, 2). Dates are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: 6.1 Build calendar rows
6.2 Set pbi_calendar path
[7] PLAN OPT: GLIDEPATHS
info: STAGE 7 - one message per site: the folder eu_report/reference/glidepaths/site=<Site>/ is listed, the newest .csv is read and parsed, and the target lookup of the site is stored in flow context: machine-site and month (01/MM/YYYY) give the OEE target (bucket "% OEE"), the PDT target ("Planned Downtime (Total)") and the UPDT target ("Unplanned Downtime (Total)"), as the three target queries of the report do after the unpivot. A site without a file stops here and the log says so.

name: 7.1 Set glidepaths folder
7.2 Pick the file
7.3 Build target lookup
[8] PLAN OPT: SHIFT PATTERNS
info: STAGE 8 - the Shift Patterns file (eu_report/reference/shift_naming/site=All/) is listed, read and parsed, and the lookup raw shift name to Shift is stored in flow context (the report joins ShiftName to the Shift Type column and keeps the Shift; an unknown name gives an empty shift).

name: 8.1 Set shift folder
8.2 Pick the file
8.3 Build shift lookup
[9] PLAN OPT: MONTHS
info: STAGE 9 - the month files of the site (eu_report/pbi_report/source/plan_opt/site=<Site>/plan_opt_YYYY-MM.csv) are listed and the months of the job that exist are chosen (a missing month is logged and skipped: a read node would stop on a missing file). One message per month, one per second.

name: 9.1 Set plan OPT folder
9.2 Choose months
[10] PLAN OPT: ROWS
info: STAGE 10 - one month of one site: the file is read and parsed, then pbi_plan_opt rows (machine and area rules of the site, shift name from the Shift Patterns file, minutes without seconds, Unique Machine Name, Product Key, the three targets of the month) and pbi_time_utilisation rows (own machine rules, sum per machine and day, minutes with seconds) are built. Out 3 is a check line: rows read, kept, left out, shifts without a mapping, machines without a target.

name: 10.1 Set month file
10.2 Build plan rows
[11] pbi_plan_opt
info: STAGE 11 - decide (nothing is written in dry-run mode or for an empty month), then parquet, the month path eu_report/pbi_report/report/pbi_plan_opt/site=<Site>/pbi_plan_opt_<YYYY-MM>.parquet and write object. A rerun replaces the month.

name: 11.1 Decide pbi_plan_opt
11.2 Set pbi_plan_opt month path
[12] pbi_time_utilisation
info: STAGE 12 - the same for pbi_time_utilisation: one row per machine and day, total, planned and OEE time summed in minutes, All Time 1440.

name: 12.1 Decide pbi_time_utilisation
12.2 Set pbi_time_utilisation month path
[13] PLAN OPT: FAILED
info: STAGE 13 - a Glidepaths or Shift Patterns file that is missing or empty: one log line, nothing is built for that site.

name: 13.1 Describe failure
[14] ERRORS
info: STAGE 14 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: 14.1 Describe error
[15] LOG
info: STAGE 15 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: 15.1 Format log line
15.2 Build log write
[16] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 16 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.

name: 16.1 Append log rows
